# SEO-039: Serve search-critical metadata in the initial server response

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| --- | --- |

| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

The title, description, canonical, and robots directives are present in the response body as it leaves the server, not injected later by client-side script after the document has loaded.

## Rationale

Directives that only appear after script execution are absent from the first fetch, and any consumer that reads the response without running the page's JavaScript sees a document with no metadata at all.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "client_rendered",
    "javascript_app"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Move metadata resolution into whichever server phase already produces the document shell - the framework's head API, a server route handler, or the prerender step. Do not keep a client-side fallback that writes the same tags again, because two writers produce duplicate elements.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Fetch the route without executing JavaScript and diff the metadata elements found there against the same elements in the rendered document.
- Evidence: `RAW_HTML`, `RENDERED_HTML`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`, `AI_ASSISTANT_RETRIEVAL`
- Frameworks: `react-spa`, `vite`, `next-app-router`, `next-pages-router`, `astro`, `remix`, `sveltekit`, `nuxt`
- Caution: none recorded.
